h1: Urbanization and the Impact on Children's Play in India

props.title: Urbanization and the Impact on Children's Play in India
props.summaryText: As Indian cities grow, children's play is squeezed: less space, more traffic, more screens. What has changed, and what planners, builders, schools and parents can do about it.
props.author: meera-iyer
props.imageAlt: High-rise residential towers in an Indian city

takeaways.text: Urban growth has taken much of the informal space children used to play in.
Traffic and safety concerns keep children indoors and close to home.
Smaller homes and busy schedules push play towards screens and structured activities.
Planned play spaces in every neighbourhood and housing project are now essential.

faq.q: How does urbanisation affect children's play?
faq.a: It reduces open and informal play spaces, increases traffic and safety concerns, shrinks homes, and fills children's time with travel, classes and screens, so children play outdoors less and in more restricted ways.

faq.q: What can cities do to support children's play?
faq.a: Plan play spaces close to homes, protect parks and open land, make streets safer, open school grounds to communities, and maintain existing playgrounds.
